prompt: We're setting up a NATO SECRET-level shared infrastructure for a multinational defense project involving Norway, Denmark, and Germany. Each nation has different national security requirements but we need to process NATO SECRET data on a common platform. The infrastructure will be hosted in a LIST-X equivalent facility in Norway. We need to handle both NATO-classified and nationally-classified data from the three participating nations, with proper separation. How do we architect this considering the different national frameworks, NATO requirements, and the need for cross-domain data sharing between national enclaves?

assertions.name: nato_classification_correct
assertions.description: Correctly lists NATO classification levels (NATO RESTRICTED through COSMIC TOP SECRET)

assertions.name: nsm_norway_authority
assertions.description: Identifies NSM (Nasjonal Sikkerhetsmyndighet) as Norway's national security authority

assertions.name: bsi_germany_authority
assertions.description: Identifies BSI as Germany's relevant security authority for IT systems

assertions.name: cfcs_denmark_authority
assertions.description: Identifies CFCS (Center for Cybersikkerhed) as Denmark's relevant authority

assertions.name: national_enclave_separation
assertions.description: Designs separate enclaves for each nation's nationally-classified data, with NATO SECRET as the shared tier

assertions.name: nato_crypto_requirement
assertions.description: Specifies that NATO-approved cryptographic products are required for NATO-classified data

assertions.name: cross_domain_between_enclaves
assertions.description: Addresses controlled data flow between national enclaves and the NATO tier (guards, CDS, release procedures)

assertions.name: bilateral_security_agreements
assertions.description: Mentions need for bilateral or multilateral security agreements between participating nations

assertions.name: personnel_clearance_multinational
assertions.description: Addresses that personnel need both national clearance AND NATO clearance, and that access to another nation's data requires specific authorization

assertions.name: red_black_separation
assertions.description: Addresses red/black separation or TEMPEST considerations for NATO SECRET processing

assertions.name: ncia_accreditation
assertions.description: Mentions NCIA (NATO Communications and Information Agency) role in accreditation of NATO systems

assertions.name: physical_security_facility
assertions.description: Addresses facility security requirements (LIST-X or equivalent, physical access controls, inspection requirements)
